addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

name: ios

# Its own workflow, not a job in test.yml, purely so it can be path-filtered.
# GitHub only supports `paths` at the workflow level, and macOS runners bill at
# roughly ten times the Linux rate: most pull requests here touch no Swift at
# all, so running this on them would spend the plan's minutes for nothing.
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - "ios/**"
      - ".github/workflows/ios.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "ios/**"
      - ".github/workflows/ios.yml"

jobs:
  ios-test:
    runs-on: self-hosted-mac
    # A hung simulator boot is the usual failure here, and the default 6 hour
    # timeout would bill all of it at the macOS rate for a job of minutes.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ios
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # A resolve or build failure below does not say which Xcode produced it.
      - run: xcodebuild -version

      - run: brew install xcodegen

      # The .xcodeproj is git-ignored, so a fresh checkout has no project yet.
      - run: xcodegen generate

      # Package versions live in project.yml, so that is the cache key. It
      # pins ranges rather than exact versions, so a restored cache can be
      # stale; xcodebuild re-resolves what it needs, which is why the loose
      # restore-keys fallback is safe.
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ios/.spm-cache
          key: ios-spm-${{ hashFiles('ios/project.yml') }}
          restore-keys: ios-spm-

      # Resolving a device at runtime instead of hardcoding a name: GitHub's
      # macOS image ships a different simulator set than any dev machine, and
      # the set changes with every image bump.
      - name: Pick a simulator
        run: |
          udid=$(xcrun simctl list devices available --json | jq -r '
            .devices
            | to_entries
            | map(select(.key | test("SimRuntime\\.iOS")))
            | sort_by(.key | [scan("[0-9]+") | tonumber])
            | map(.value[])
            | map(select(.name | startswith("iPhone")))
            | last | .udid // ""
          ')
          if [ -z "$udid" ]; then
            echo "No available iPhone simulator on this runner" >&2
            # An unavailable runtime, and why, shows up here and nowhere else.
            xcrun simctl list runtimes >&2
            xcrun simctl list devices available >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIMULATOR_UDID=$udid" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Raw xcodebuild output on purpose. The run logs expected Clerk keychain
      # errors (OSStatus -34018, no entitlement without code signing), and a
      # formatter pipe would also cost us xcodebuild's exit code.
      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          xcodebuild test -project Haven.xcodeproj -scheme Haven \
            -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$SIMULATOR_UDID" \
            -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath .spm-cache \
            CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO

name: test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: self-hosted-mac
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
        env:
          # The convex tests stub all network calls, but the OpenAI client
          # asserts a key exists before the stubbed fetch is ever reached.
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ci-dummy-key-network-is-mocked
      - run: npm run build

name: Claude

# Interactive bot: reacts when you write "@claude" in an issue,
# a PR comment, or a review. Ask it to implement, fix, or explain.
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review:
    types: [submitted]
  issues:
    types: [opened, assigned]

jobs:
  claude:
    if: |
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review' && contains(github.event.review.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && (contains(github.event.issue.body, '@claude') || contains(github.event.issue.title, '@claude')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Claude Code
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}

name: Claude Daily Review

# Scheduled bot: every morning Claude proposes ONE safe improvement by editing
# files; a deterministic step then opens a pull request with those changes.
on:
  schedule:
    # 13:08 UTC = ~6:08am America/Los_Angeles during PDT (shifts 1h after DST).
    - cron: '8 13 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch: {}

jobs:
  daily-review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Claude proposes one improvement
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          claude_args: '--max-turns 120'
          prompt: |
            You are a daily code-improvement bot for this repository (a Vite +
            TypeScript app with a Convex backend and an iOS folder). Your ONLY job
            this run is to propose ONE improvement by EDITING FILES.

            1. Read only what you need: README.md, CLAUDE.md, todo.md, and the
               files relevant to the change you pick. Do not read the whole repo.
            2. Make ONE small, safe, high-confidence improvement by editing files in
               the working tree — a real bug, a performance win, a security issue,
               or a UX fix. Keep the diff under ~150 changed lines. No sweeping
               refactors.
            3. Validate lightly if relevant (for example `npx tsc --noEmit`).
            4. DO NOT use git. Do NOT commit, push, create a branch, or open a PR.
               Only edit files in place — a later automated step handles the PR.
            5. ALWAYS write a file named `CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md` at the repository root:
               - First line, exactly: `TITLE: <concise pull request title>`
               - Then a blank line, then the description: the problem, the fix, the
                 category (bug/perf/security/UX), files touched, what you validated,
                 and a short "how to test".
               - If you genuinely found NO safe change and edited nothing, instead
                 make the first line exactly `TITLE: NO_CHANGE` and below it explain
                 what you examined and why nothing was safe to change today.

      - name: Prepare PR content
        id: prep
        run: |
          if [ ! -f CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md ]; then
            {
              echo "## Claude Daily Review"
              echo "Claude did not produce CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md. See the \"Claude proposes one improvement\" step log."
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "make_pr=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          TITLE="$(sed -n '1s/^TITLE: //p' CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md)"
          tail -n +2 CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md > "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr_body.md"
          # Always surface Claude's write-up on the run's Summary page.
          {
            echo "## Claude Daily Review"
            echo "**${TITLE}**"
            echo ""
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/pr_body.md"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # Remove the helper file so it is NOT part of the PR diff.
          rm -f CLAUDE_PR_BODY.md
          if [ "$TITLE" = "NO_CHANGE" ] || [ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
            echo "No PR opened (title='$TITLE', changed files=$(git status --porcelain | wc -l | tr -d ' '))."
            echo "make_pr=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "make_pr=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "title=$TITLE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Open Pull Request
        if: steps.prep.outputs.make_pr == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v7
        with:
          base: main
          branch: claude/auto-${{ github.run_id }}
          title: ${{ steps.prep.outputs.title }}
          body-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/pr_body.md
          commit-message: ${{ steps.prep.outputs.title }}
          author: "Claude Daily Bot <claude-bot@users.noreply.github.com>"
          committer: "Claude Daily Bot <claude-bot@users.noreply.github.com>"
          delete-branch: false

content.text: I have enough context. Both changed workflows switch from GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners to `self-hosted-mac`, and both trigger on `pull_request`, with no gating on the PR author's association (no `if: github.event.pull_request.author_association in ('OWNER', 'MEMBER', 'COLLABORATOR')`, no `pull_request_target` + trusted-branch pattern, no manual-approval environment). This is the canonical GitHub-warned self-hosted-runner + PR trigger anti-pattern, and it exists on BOTH changed files.

findings.vulnerableCode:
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: self-hosted-mac
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build
findings.explanation: The + line switches this job from the ephemeral GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner to a persistent `self-hosted-mac` runner while the workflow still fires on the unrestricted `pull_request` event with no author-association gate, no `pull_request_target` + trusted-branch pattern, and no protected-environment approval. On a self-hosted runner every step becomes arbitrary code execution on the runner host controlled by whoever opened the PR: `npm ci` runs install/postinstall scripts from a PR-controlled `package.json` / `package-lock.json`, `npm test` and `npm run build` execute PR-controlled source. Unlike GitHub-hosted runners, the machine is not destroyed after the job: an attacker's PR can drop persistent implants in the runner service's home dir, poison the `~/.npm` cache that `setup-node@v5 cache: npm` restores for subsequent trusted runs, read any secrets/SSH keys/browser cookies on the host Mac, and pivot into any network the runner sits on. GitHub explicitly warns: "We recommend that you only use self-hosted runners with private repositories. This is because forks of your public repository can potentially run dangerous code on your self-hosted runner machine by creating a pull request that executes the code in a workflow." Even if the repo is currently private, any collaborator (or compromised collaborator account) gains code execution on the runner host with no review gate. First-time-contributor approval only gates the FIRST run — once approved, subsequent PRs from that account execute automatically.
findings.fix: Either (a) revert to `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` for `pull_request` runs, or (b) restrict the job to trusted authors with a gate such as `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(fromJSON('["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.pull_request.author_association)`, and additionally require a protected `environment:` with required reviewers so untrusted PRs cannot execute. Also configure the runner as ephemeral (`--ephemeral`) or run it inside a throwaway VM/container per job so cache/workspace state cannot leak across runs.

findings.vulnerableCode:
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths:
      - "ios/**"
      - ".github/workflows/ios.yml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "ios/**"
      - ".github/workflows/ios.yml"

jobs:
  ios-test:
    runs-on: self-hosted-mac
    ...
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - run: brew install xcodegen
      - run: xcodegen generate
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ios/.spm-cache
          key: ios-spm-${{ hashFiles('ios/project.yml') }}
          restore-keys: ios-spm-
      - run: |
          xcodebuild test -project Haven.xcodeproj -scheme Haven ...
findings.explanation: Same self-hosted-runner-on-pull_request anti-pattern as test.yml, and arguably worse: the `xcodegen generate` step reads a PR-controlled `ios/project.yml` and emits an Xcode project, and `xcodebuild test` then executes the resulting project — Xcode targets can carry arbitrary Run Script build phases and SwiftPM packages/plugins that run code at resolve time. A PR touching `ios/**` (which is exactly what the path filter allows) can therefore run arbitrary shell as the runner user on the maintainer's Mac. The `actions/cache@v4` step compounds this: the cache key `ios-spm-${{ hashFiles('ios/project.yml') }}` plus the loose `restore-keys: ios-spm-` fallback means a malicious PR can populate the SwiftPM cache with poisoned sources that a subsequent legitimate `main` build will happily restore and compile/execute — a classic cache-poisoning pivot from PR to trusted branch. `brew install xcodegen` is also mutable global host state. None of this is safe under the current lack of author-association gating or protected-environment approval.
findings.fix: Gate the `pull_request` execution behind trusted-author check and/or a required-reviewer `environment:`; keep untrusted PRs on `macos-latest`. Namespace/scope the cache key with `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name` so PR runs cannot write to the cache namespace used by `main`, or skip `actions/cache` entirely on PR-triggered runs. Configure the self-hosted runner as ephemeral (fresh VM per job) so `brew`, `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData`, and workspace files cannot persist between runs.
